Definition: Holy, set apart and sacred — describing God's utter distinctness and purity, and people or things consecrated to Him.
BiblicalUsage: Seraphim cry 'Holy, holy, holy' before God's throne, and Israel is called to be holy because God is holy. Qadosh marks what belongs to God and must be treated with reverence and purity.
TheologicalSignificance: God's holiness is not distant coldness — the Holy One of Israel draws near to redeem. His call 'be holy, for I am holy' is an invitation into His own character.
